title: India markets: the daily wrap
dek: How the Nifty 50 and Sensex opened and closed each trading day, the overnight gap, and the reasons reporters gave.
seoTitle: Sensex and Nifty today: open, close and gap, day by day
status: Rises above 25,500 for first time since February

glance.what: The Nifty 50 closed at 25,514.30 on 19 November, up 1.14% and above 25,500 for the first time since 26 February, according to Business Today. Over eight sessions since the Diwali Muhurat trading close on 8 November, it is up from 24,986.40.
glance.why: Reporters credited buying in auto, bank and consumer goods stocks, helped by falling metal prices, which lower costs for carmakers. IT stocks fell after US Federal Reserve minutes pointed to more US rate rises. A day earlier, profit booking had pulled the index down 0.63%.
glance.next: Markets are shut on 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti. The RBI's next policy meeting runs 2 to 4 December.

forYou: If you own an index fund or ETF that tracks the Nifty 50 or Sensex, its value moves roughly in step with these numbers. A gap at the open usually reflects news that broke while Indian markets were shut, such as overnight moves on Wall Street. This is information, not investment advice.

upcoming.label: 24 Nov
upcoming.text: Markets closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti

next: Watch foreign investor flows, oil prices and the dollar.

events.title: Gap up at the open, then gives back most of it
events.summary: The Nifty 50 opened 90 points higher on positive global cues and buying in banks and financial stocks, IANS reports, but drifted down through the day to close 58.25 points up. HDFC Sky says both indices still posted their highest close since 27 February, though more shares fell than rose.

events.title: Markets shut for Diwali Balipratipada
events.summary: The NSE and BSE were closed on Tuesday for Diwali Balipratipada, a listed trading holiday. Trading resumed on Wednesday.

events.title: Big gap up after the holiday; Nifty ends 0.84% higher
events.summary: Returning from the holiday, the Nifty opened 293.15 points higher, a bigger jump than early overseas trading had pointed to, HDFC Sky reports. It eased from the open but closed up 210.40 points. DSIJ credits foreign investor buying, lower crude oil prices and buying in public sector bank and auto shares; Mahindra & Mahindra rose 5.30% while ICICI Bank fell 1.10%.

events.title: Opens lower after Nvidia's slide, recovers to a small gain
events.summary: Indian shares opened in the red as Nvidia fell in US after-hours trading on reports its board could oust CEO Jensen Huang, India TV reports. Banks and financial stocks led a recovery, helped by foreign buying and softer oil, and the Nifty closed 44.30 points up. Shriram Finance (+3.6%) and Bajaj Finance (+3.4%) gained; Nestle India (−2.1%) fell. The rupee weakened 34 paise to 94.03 per dollar, HDFC Sky reports.
events.status: Market data · India TV, HDFC Sky
events.differs: Deccan Chronicle gave the Sensex open as 81,827.20; India TV and Upstox give 81,762.27. Upstox's closing report headline gives the Nifty close as 25,229; HDFC Sky gives 25,299.35, which matches the reported 44.30-point gain.

events.title: Gap down as inflation crosses 6%; Nifty falls 155 points
events.summary: The Nifty opened 89.50 points lower and kept falling after October retail inflation came in at 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% upper limit, HDFC Sky reports. Upstox also cites weak global markets, higher US bond yields and rising oil. The Nifty closed at 25,144.30, ending a three-day winning run; Shriram Finance was the biggest loser.

events.title: Opens higher despite Wall Street's fall; Nifty Bank hits a record
events.summary: The Nifty opened 61.85 points higher even though US shares had fallen, and closed up 146.80 points. HDFC Sky credits record foreign investor buying, easing crude oil and buying in FMCG and bank stocks, as money moved away from AI-linked trades elsewhere in Asia. The Nifty Bank index closed at a record 61,576, CNBC-TV18 reports; Max Healthcare was the top Nifty gainer, per Upstox.
events.differs: HDFC Sky gives the Sensex close as 82,102.85 (+510.40); Upstox, Kotak Neo and Zee Business give 82,104.79 (+512.34).

events.title: Flat open, then a steady climb as banks and realty lead
events.summary: The Nifty opened 13.80 points lower, close to flat, then rose through the day to close up 96.30 points, Liquide reports. Kotak Neo credits lower crude prices and foreign buying. Realty (+1.94%) and financial stocks led; Bank Nifty rose 1.13%. Adani Enterprises (+3.24%) and Eicher Motors (+3.01%) were top gainers; HCL Technologies fell 2.09%.

events.title: Profit booking ends a two-day rise; metals and Titan drag
events.summary: The Nifty opened 64.25 points lower and closed down 159.45 points (0.63%) at 25,227.95, according to DSIJ and Angel One. The Sensex fell 500.38 points (0.61%) to 82,031.81. HDFC Sky and Kotak Neo say investors booked profits after a strong November rally. HDFC Sky says a stronger US dollar and expectations of more US rate rises hurt metal prices. Thirteen of 16 sector indices fell, HDFC Sky reports: consumer durables lost about 3% and metals about 2.5%. Titan fell 5.3%, the worst in the Nifty; SBI (+2.4%) and Cipla (+2%) were the top gainers.
events.differs: Kotak Neo gives the Nifty close as 25,277.95, which does not match its own fall of 0.63% (about 160 points); DSIJ, Angel One and HDFC Sky give 25,227.95.

events.title: Autos and banks lift Nifty above 25,500 after a weak start
events.summary: The Nifty opened lower and closed up 286.35 points (1.14%) at 25,514.30, according to Business Today and Kotak Neo. The Sensex rose 989.94 points (1.21%) to 83,021.75. Business Today says it was the Nifty's first close above 25,500 since 26 February. Marketcalls says the market started lower after minutes from the US Federal Reserve pointed to more US rate rises, then autos, banks and consumer goods stocks pulled it up. Business Today and Kotak Neo say falling copper and other metal prices should lower costs for carmakers and appliance makers. The Nifty Auto index rose 4.40% and Nifty IT fell 1.10%, per Kotak Neo and Marketcalls. Maruti Suzuki gained 7.30%, the best in the Nifty; Infosys (−1.52%) fell the most, per Marketcalls.
events.status: Market data · Business Today, Kotak Neo
events.differs: Only Liquide gives an opening level (25,186, about 42 points lower); the other reports say only that the market opened lower. Marketcalls says the Nifty slipped below 25,150 in early trade. Business Today gives Nifty Bank's close as 62,081.30 (with 63,063 as its intraday record); Marketcalls gives 63,063.00 as the close.
